description: Move an owned object off the lot into your inventory. Prerequisite: you are the owner of the target object (VMTSOObjectState.OwnerID == you; handler-side gate). Object must be user-movable. Effect: the object disappears from nearby_objects and appears in your inventory (query-inventory) with its current state preserved (upgrade level, wear, etc.). Cost: none (no money moves; this is the 'refund to inventory' path, distinct from delete-object's 'refund to money' path). Wire: VMNetSendToInventoryCmd on the lot Aries socket.
call_signatures: cf $CF send-to-inventory --target_object_persist_id <object's persist_id>                             # object-owner only (distinct from lot-owner!)
common_mistakes: Non-object-owner → ok:false ('caller is not the object owner') — lot-owner alone is not enough.
target_object_persist_id is a persist_id (uint) of the OBJECT, not a lot or avatar persist id.
Object not found in local VM → ok:false ('not found in local VM').
perception_hints: Your balance (can you afford the object?): perception.balance
Am I the owner? perception.lot.owner_is_me — owner-only ops refuse otherwise
Free tile to place on: inspect perception.nearby_objects[] to find unoccupied tiles; positions are in tile coords, multiply by 16 for subtile x/y
refuse_conditions: missing target_object_persist_id → ok:false with 'requires target_object_persist_id (uint, non-zero)'
object not found in local VM → ok:false with 'object persist_id=<n> not found in local VM'
caller is not the object owner → ok:false with 'caller is not the object owner (object_owner=..., me=...)'
